messages:
Anna: Heads-up, long-context runs (32k+) on H100 canaries show steady GPU mem growth when kv paging is enabled. Suspect page-table reuse bug.

Mike: Which model/config and repro cmd?

Anna: repro: `./infer_bench --model rdx-7b --ctx 32768 --batch 1 --kv-paging=on`
Log tail: 
```
[INFO] alloc_page page=0x7fbc12 size=2MB gpu=H100-8
[INFO] evict_page page=0x7fbbf4 freed=1
[INFO] alloc_page page=0x7fbc12 size=2MB gpu=H100-8
[INFO] kv_map_install slot=2112 page=0x7fbc12
[WARN] kv_map_install slot=2112 page=0x7fbbf4  <-- installing stale pointer
```
Evict log shows freed=1 but later the same physical addr is seen in installs.

Jyoti: We see similar on A100 but pattern is plateau+jump. H100 is linear growth for us.

Sam: Any cuda-memcheck or allocator-race output?

Anna: KV_ALLOC_RACE=1 emitted concurrent-free warnings. cuda-memcheck reported one invalid read in paged_attn_lookup kernel (kernel stack points to paged_attn_kernel.cu around kv lookup).

Lee: Instrumented page-table ops locally. Root cause looks like non-atomic read-modify-write on the dense page map. Evict and install can race: evict clears pointer then fast alloc reuses same page; another thread observing the map during the window can see the old pointer -> ABA/double-install.

Mike: That matches the per-GPU slab stats: H100 shows build-up of orphan entries (never returned to global pool). If evict isn't fully visible, allocator produces garbage.

Anna: Perf counters we grabbed: H100 shows high coherent atomic rate and L2 traffic. A100 has lower atomics but many small free fragments -> fragmentation rather than continuous leak.

Sam: Note kernel selection: H100 uses warp-batched paged kernel which batches map updates per-warp. That kernel assumes installs are single-writer per slot. Our current batching heuristics can produce parallel installs to same slot.

Jyoti: Also large batch sizes exacerbate this: many concurrent kv installs for adjacent slots. Batcher heuristics may need guardrails when paging enabled.

Lee: Short-term mitigation: limit max batch size when kv-paging is on, and fallback warp-batched -> lane-serial installs on H100 canaries. That reduces throughput but avoids races.

Mike: Long-term fix proposal: epoch-based retire + CAS install:
- Add 32-bit epoch/version per page.
- On eviction increment epoch and move page to retire queue.
- Install uses atomic CAS on packed (ptr|epoch) to avoid ABA.
- Reclaimer reclaims after global quiesce.
This prevents seeing resurrected pointers.

Anna: I prototyped epoch+CAS locally. 6h smoke run with 32k context showed no mem growth. Need A100 and older-gen validation + quant path tests.

Lee: Implementation notes: pack ptr low bits (aligned) with u32 epoch, use atomic compare_exchange_weak on 64-bit word (ptr|epoch). Add unit test to simulate N-thread evict/install interleaving.

Sam: CI tests to add: stress.long_ctx.32k (H100,A100), race.eviction_install (multi-threaded synthetic), perf.guard (L2/atomic counters baseline), quant.q4 path verification. Also gate allocator-race-detect in CI.

build-bot: CI run started for branch kv/epoch-pagemap (PR #2412) with stress + q4 matrix.

Jyoti: Rollout plan: land to canary but keep kv-paging disabled on H100 canaries until metrics stable. Consider leaving paging off on H100 in prod until we validate across driver versions.

Mike: Also add runtime flag --kv-paging-serial for canary to force serial installs for easier repro/debug.

deploy-bot: Action scheduled: disable kv-paging on dedicated-h100-canary at 2026-02-02T02:00Z; alerts hooked to GPU mem and L2 atomics.

Anna: Notes: quantized kernels use different KV layout and allocator paths. Include Q4 runs as these exercise alternate alloc sizes and may hit different plumbing.

Lee: I'll open follow-up to land CAS+epoch+tests. Also add targeted unit that reproduces ABA in user-mode with fake pages to catch regressions.

Sam: Parallel ask: verify kernel selection path honors atomic-safe install primitive; if not, switch H100 warp-batched paged kernel to lane-serial install until proven safe.

Mike: Thanks. Please paste PRs and perf graphs here when available. :thumbsup:
